lines: Don't leave me alone in the Bamboo Jungle. Everything rustles like it is sneaking up on me.
The Bamboo Jungle is too dense to lose sight of you in. I could barely tell which way was safe.
I was stuck in the Bamboo Jungle listening to every stalk creak and every branch snap.
If you disappear in a Bamboo Jungle, all I have left is noise and bad guesses.
The bamboo kept moving, and I could not tell what was wind and what was trouble.
Every direction looked the same once you were gone.
Please do not leave me somewhere that can hide you after three steps.
The Bamboo Jungle made every little sound feel too close.
I kept trying to see through the stalks, but the jungle was better at hiding things than I was at finding them.
I was alone in all that green noise, hoping the next rustle was you coming back.
Don't leave me in the Jungle. I cannot tell whether the next sound is leaves or teeth.
The Jungle is too thick to lose your guide in. I could barely see a safe way forward.
I was stranded in the Jungle with vines everywhere and no clear line back to you.
If you disappear in a Jungle, I am left with heat, noise, and no honest path.
The vines made every route feel slower than it should have been.
I kept hearing things move above me, beside me, and somewhere I could not see.
Please do not leave me somewhere that turns every step into a guess.
The Jungle was loud enough to hide danger and dense enough to hide you.
I could not tell if I should call out or stay quiet, and neither felt safe.
I was sweating, lost, and trying not to imagine what might be watching from the leaves.
Don't leave me in the Mangrove Swamp. Mud, roots, and shallow water slow everything down.
The Mangrove Swamp is too tangled to stand alone in with any confidence.
I waited in the Mangrove Swamp trying not to trip over roots while listening for danger.
If you disappear in a Mangrove Swamp, I am left ankle-deep in worry and swamp water.
The roots caught at my feet every time I tried to move.
I could not tell where the path ended and the swamp started.
Please do not leave me somewhere the ground argues with every step.
The mud made running feel impossible, which made waiting feel worse.
The Mangrove Swamp hid too much under the water and too much between the roots.
I was stuck in the muck, watching the trees and hoping you had not forgotten me.
Don't leave me in the Sparse Jungle. Fewer trees do not make it feel much safer.
The Sparse Jungle still has enough brush to hide trouble while I wait for you.
I stood in the Sparse Jungle trying to decide which rustle mattered most.
If you disappear in a Sparse Jungle, I am left with heat, brush, and too many maybes.
There was just enough open space to make me feel visible and just enough cover to make me nervous.
I kept looking between the trees, hoping one of them would give you back.
Please do not leave me somewhere that looks open but still hides too much.
The Sparse Jungle made every sound feel like it had somewhere to hide.
I could see farther than in a thick jungle, but not far enough to relax.
I was alone in the heat, listening to the brush and trying not to guess wrong.
Don't leave me in the Swamp. Mud, <aqua><wavy>water</wavy></aqua>, and gloom make a miserable watch post.
The Swamp is too soggy and too murky to be standing alone in.
I waited in the Swamp trying not to trip into the water while I looked for you.
If you disappear in a Swamp, I am left wading through mud and bad feelings.
Every step made a sound I did not want anything else to hear.
The water was shallow enough to cross and deep enough to make me nervous.
Please do not leave me somewhere the ground feels half-finished.
The Swamp made everything smell wet, old, and unfriendly.
I kept watching the water, because I could not tell what was under it.
I was alone in the muck, hoping the next movement was you and not something worse.
